## UNCERTAIN ITEMS

- INS Module 5 includes a Firewall teaching sequence that is not listed in the core application set (SSL/TLS, WLAN, GSM/UMTS, payments, broadcast, eID, home). Marked supplementary where detected.
- International Business Module 6 is a shorter V8 deck (6 content slides). Subtopics are the actual slide titles; later V9 expansion may add teaching depth.
- Topic-level hours are Estimated even when a module has a source-defined total; Java (9/8/9/8/8), BDA (40), Parallel Computing (40), IB Module 4 (7) and IB Module 5 (6) module budgets were used as allocation targets.
- Program/Semester left blank unless present in the registry or syllabus extract (Java semester 3, BDA/PC semester VII, Deep Learning BCA semester 7, IB MBA).
- INS, TOC, DBMS, Chemistry, RM-IPR and OS do not have full official syllabus text files in-repo comparable to BIS701/BCS702/1BCS302; module titles and slide kickers were the primary structure.
- Computer Networks-I uses Unit 1–8 (10CS55 / Forouzan), not a 5-module VTU split.
- Chemistry and Deep Learning slide counts are high because decks are beat-level; subtopics were clustered from story/syllabus checkpoints rather than one row per slide.

## METHOD

1. Read subject registry in `src/data/subjects.jsx`.
2. Extract slide id/title/kicker/section from each live module source (JSX/JSON/Java meta).
3. Drop presentation mechanics (openers, journeys, recap banks, PYQ/resource slides).
4. Reconstruct Topic ← kicker/section or official syllabus checkpoint; Subtopic ← clustered teaching titles.
5. Allocate 1–2 hour units toward source module hour budgets when known.
